knowledge_learned: The units digit is the remainder modulo 10. The units digit of a sum or product can be found by doing the operation on the operands’ units digits and taking the result modulo 10.
Repeated multiplication produces recurring units digits. Positive powers of a base ending in 3 cycle through 3, 9, 7, and 1, so an exponent divisible by four gives units digit 1.
Bases with equal units digits have equal units digits when raised to the same positive integer power.
mechanics_observed: Compare result endings without calculating complete sums or products.
Apply the same shortcut to a sum with several terms, a square, and then a large power.
Reapply the power shortcut with a different base that has the same units digit.
